reviews.text: Waiting for the English translation to be released in full but I played the demo extensively and enjoyed what it had to offer in terms of story, characters and build diversity. Edit* After playing through once, I had an enjoyable time despite not being able to read a great load of the story. The game is well-balanced and each enemy is unique with a specific fighting style in mind. There is a powerful equipment accessible very early in the game which allowed me to beat many fights with little difficulty except for the last two fights of my run. [spoiler]Scarlet is a beast and gravity is just cheap.[/spoiler] The upgrade system for equipment was a great addition, it allows you to take equipment that would have been power-crept and improve their stats and their abilities. There's no need to worry too much over your combos not being able to keep up with the increasing numbers. Build diversity from the demo was definitely expanded as there were so many items you can obtain and buy, I had too much money since I was satisfied with what I obtained within the first month though. The translation quality is great, ignoring minor typos. I speak from the perspective of someone who reads a lot for enjoyment and very picky on text writing. The characterization of the characters were done well and there is a very large cast, though the interactions are brief. There is a very large number of endings as well, which I am guessing you are locked to one per playthrough. The game is intended to be played several times and it shows as the skip button skips at a very fast speed, battles are very quick and the progression system hardly drags you back. I look forward to enjoying the story properly and I can tell a lot of care was put into the game considering how characters will point out if you have met them before (in which there are multiple ways to meet some characters), are wearing cute clothing [spoiler]Emma[/spoiler], and Even a special story if you know what to do in the first few days of the game. There is some fine-tuning to the interaction branches I mentioned before but that can be easily fixed as players point it out to the developers. Edit** Story was cute as I thought it'd be. The characters I can now understand were lovable that it was a shame the game is too short. Translation quality was great, number of typos I've encountered are slightly over what I can count with my hands but they don't get in the way too much. Some regrets I have with the game is with how powerful some of the final bosses are, I am not sure whether not going for the strongest gift in the Waste area is viable if you want to get the win ending on a run (***It's possible but it will be close). And being limited in time, you aren't able to complete every route in the game before the final tournament, where with each completion, you get a special buff and your friends cheering you on at the final.

[h1][b]Robot Girl’s Dream: A Gritty Little Heart in a Shiny Steel Shell[/b][/h1] "Who knew robo-feels and mech brawls could hit this hard? This is the indie sleeper that lowkey punches you in the circuits." [h1][b][1] Intro : [/b][/h1] Robot Girl's Dream -RobotBattleChampionship- is what happens when cozy slice-of-life storytelling gets fused with high-octane robot tournaments and emotional existentialism. You play as a memory-wiped android girl navigating a near-future city full of charming weirdos—both metal and meatbag. It’s half battle sim, half friendship-builder, and 100% indie heart. Don’t let the soft art fool you—underneath is a game that asks you to think, plan, and maybe cry just a little. [h1][b][2] Game Experience : [/b][/h1] Let’s start with vibes. Robot Girl’s Dream hits you with an adorable pixel style and a melancholy premise—robot girl wakes up in a junkyard with no memories, sees a battle tournament on TV, and goes “yo, I want in.” That’s your hook. From there, it becomes a beautifully branching RPG about fighting, bonding, and figuring out who the hell you are. The daily loop gives you one action per in-game day—work, explore, train, or socialize. Every choice nudges you toward one of the MANY endings (and yes, there are plenty of bad ones if you fumble). You’ll meet an eccentric lineup of NPCs—humans, androids, and the “is that a vending machine with an attitude?” tier of weird—and your interactions build up “Unison Circuits,” aka affection meters that actually boost your stats. It’s part dating sim, part JRPG grind, and the game leans into both in charming ways. Now for the combat: it’s real-time turn-based. Yep, you read that right. It plays like an Active Time Battle system where you’re constantly weighing whether to go for heavy attacks with long cooldowns or spam lighter hits. Layer in buffs, debuffs, and timing your blocks like you’re cosplaying as a 2D mecha Souls game, and the system sings. Boss fights? Brutal. Final matches? Chef’s kiss. Every victory feels earned. Customization is a major win here. You’re not just upgrading numbers—you’re visually and mechanically modding your robo-girl with new arms, legs, heads, and weapons. It’s part dress-up, part optimization sim, and totally satisfying when you find a loadout that both looks and hits right. But it’s not all circuits and sunshine. The game’s biggest enemy? The save system. Only autosaves. No manual slots. That means you screw up a choice or go into a boss under-geared? You're boned. Some players found ways around it (manual backups), but that shouldn’t be necessary. It’s a blemish on an otherwise impressively thoughtful design. [h2][b][3] Pros and Cons : [/b][/h2] [b](+) The Good Stuff / What Rocked / Why You'll Love It:[/b] [list] [*]Combat is fresh and strategic – ATB-style robot duels with real weight and tension. [*]Robust customization – Swap limbs, weapons, and outfits. Visual + mechanical changes? Let’s go. [*]Emotionally resonant storytelling – Surprisingly touching with legit twists and strong writing. [*]Replayability through the roof – Dozens of endings, branching events, hidden buffs, and secrets. [*]Quirky world + characters – From sweet humans to sassy robots, everyone’s got a story to tell. [/list] [b](-) The Bad Stuff / What Sucked / Why You Might Rage:[/b] [list] [*]No manual saves – Huge pain for perfectionists. One wrong click? You’re restarting the whole dang run. [*]Can get grindy – Optimizing builds and chasing true endings needs time and planning. [*]UI bugs + rare crashes – A few players hit freezes or UI lockups. Patch needed. [*]Lack of gallery/replay features – Unlock an ending? Good luck seeing it again without rerunning the game. [*]Some event conditions are too vague – Miss a flag early and you're locked out of whole routes. [/list] [h2][b][4] Final Thoughts / The Verdict : [/b][/h2] Robot Girl’s Dream is a love letter to old-school RPG mechanics and emotional sci-fi stories, dressed up with adorable sprite art and deceptively deep gameplay. It's short enough for a weekend binge, but packed with enough depth to justify multiple playthroughs. If you can stomach the janky save system and love a good underdog fight-to-the-top narrative, this one's absolutely worth booting up. Final Score: 8.2/10 — “Think Persona meets Megaman Legends with one save slot and robo-feels.” [h2][b][5] Side Note / Shameless Plug : [/b][/h2] Digging heartfelt indie gems with quirky characters and tough boss fights? Hit up our [u][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/33855818]Nyanco Channel[/url][/u] review feed for more unsung bangers and emotionally confusing robot adventures. Also: if your robot has a ponytail and dual scythes, you’re legally obligated to drop a follow. You know who you are. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3466920575

I really wish Steam would start bumping games like this up after they receive a translation because it really doesn't feel fair for this game to have so much work put into it for all of us to enjoy and not be recognized for it. So the least I can do after spending time with this is to give a review. I recommend this game highly. Very highly. To the point where I feel it is completely worth it for the full asking price, here. If you have some sort of affinity for a time management/raising sort of game (think princess maker) with a splash of medabots-like part building and RPG combat, all wrapped up with a very cutesy style, then please, don't bother reading further. You really shouldn't hesitate and just pick this up. What I love the most about this game is how it was just made with such calculated precision. What I mean by that is that every aspect of this game bears some sort of fruit, and will funnel into one another system. For instance, you can do a string of events and get a set of powerful, fun, unique equipment (and/or cosmetic items too 🤤🤤🤤) and you bring those items into the battles. During that string of events, you might beat up some perverted cable-huffing robots and take their cores to upgrade your own parts. There's definitely that "one more turn" feeling that this game captures very well. The amount of dialogue and events is just staggering. I feel like I only barely scratched the surface of what's available in a single 8 hour playthrough, and the game is definitely set up for you to miss things on a run. But that's okay. Roll with it-- you can try different outfits and character builds, try different dialogue choices, see what characters you run into, and maybe you'll find a really neat piece of equippable gear to try on. So many of the interactions with NPCs are either insane, adorable, and sometimes just earnest (...and with that being said, it makes it hard to stomach the thought of doing an evil playthrough...) and actually engaging with these NPCs funnels directly into character power and the possibility of cool new parts to play around with. I don't even want to get started on the PARTS. Imagine how much work that was put into making a sprite unique to EVERY SINGLE PART AND HAIRSTYLE VARIATION, ALLOWING YOU TO MIX AND MATCH THEM, AND HAVING THAT BE REFLECTED BOTH IN THE VN CUTSCENES AND IN BATTLE FOR EVERY SINGLE SPRITE VARIANT OF THE MAIN CHARACTER. The thought of it is just mind blowing to me because all of this was considered and done just... For the sake of it. Reflecting your equipment is definitely mech game but for most RPGs they wouldn't even bother. Really, this is just an utterly insane thought to me. The VN style cutscenes in general are very engaging because of this mindset, too-- there's so many variations of sprites for every character, and there are a LOT of characters in this game to increase your bond level with. The game length for a playthrough is just perfect too. It allows for experimentation, for you to have fun pursuing the completion of 2-4 characters' events for the sake of their endings, and doing it all over again. This game is something special, truly. I hope that if you're reading this and you're on the fence that this may convince you to buy it, because developers like this who pour their hearts out for a passion project like this deserve so much more. I can just tell that this game was made with a lot of joy and heart.

I didn’t complete this game because it was too hard, and I didn’t want to start over. Good: -Story is good -Game looks good -Combat is good -Multiple endings -In the arena you can fight enemies to gain points. For example, if you failed a tournament and are short on points and need them to be able to enter the final tournament you can earn them here. But if you need to do that then you probably will lose the game anyway Mixed: -Tournaments get harder every time there is a new one, but you can upgrade items for a limited amount of times. Bad: -You didn’t play how the developer wanted you loose -You didn’t buy item form tv ad. Well, it turns out it’s required to beat an enemy or a boss. So, you lose or wait till it appears again on tv ad - You can upgrade items only limited amount set by developers, and some items aren’t upgradable -Some things aren’t explained. Jobs have a storyline if you work at them and you get item at the end of the job storyline -Limited amount of days so if you fail at something you lose and you can’t do every quest. -Events tied to days so you can miss some events -no game plus where you can start with items that you earned and to get different endings you have to start over to get other endings

——有大手子去联系作者汉化了，预计添加为官中，目前初翻已经完成正在进行校对—— [i]机械少女会梦见到UFC冠军吗？[/i] [i]机械少女会梦见到和人类结婚吗？[/i] [i]机械少女会梦见到组一辈子乐队吗？[/i] [i]机械少女会梦见到kirakira偶像吗？[/i] [i]机械少女会梦见到白垩纪恐龙吗？[/i] [i]机械少女会梦见到送土星人回家吗？[/i] [i]机械少女会梦见到恐怖魔鬼改造电锯人病娇吗？[/i] [i]机械少女会做梦[/i]是扮演失忆的机械少女从废品厂一路成长，三个月后在闪耀的机械人格斗大赛上挑战冠军，立志成为最强机械人的视觉小说x养成x策略游戏。 游戏模式总体上以日程安排-进入当天对应剧情-中途参加格斗大赛提高排名的模式推进。 听说是比较像《实况野球》的SUCCESS模式，但很可惜我没玩过这个，个人玩起来有点像现在的女神异闻录？ 不管怎么样，要介绍这个游戏的话首先绝对离不开的就是 [h1]太!可!爱!了![/h1] 游戏的美术风格一眼看上去就像幼稚儿童画...然而！！！事实就是如此，就是这么可爱。每个人物都有大量的表情差分（都很可爱！萌萌萌萌萌），主角这种可以换装备的成长型机娘如果替换了身体部件，也会直接反映到对话立绘中可以玩暖暖。其中除了比较正常的衣服外也有四足，轮胎腿，夹手，猩猩臂，还有像是从特摄里过来的狮子头饰胸板全甲这种很萝卜的部件。战斗立绘也是同样会很细致地反映当前装备状态。 而可爱，不止是外表！内在也很可爱100分！这是一个所有登场角色，包括反派都让人恨不起来反而觉得很可爱的世界[strike]虽然偶尔也会打个你死我活[/strike]。角色都太有个性了而且...都很可爱！光明磊落，华丽潇洒的绝对冠军斯卡雷特，有点傻傻的但还是知心大哥哥而且有事真上的亚军尼格霍斯，快乐的工厂一家人...通关后在翻阅设定集的时候我才发现剧中人物登场数量居然超过100且除极少数换色都有着立绘和自己的名字，而在20多小时的全主要路线的剧情体验中看着他们的故事没有一刻感到无聊。 我一般只能看得下去有打打杀杀的故事，而本作虽然游戏基调本身偏轻松温馨，但对话和故事发展方向都很有趣能够吸引人继续读下去。 说到这里我想着重夸赞一下这个游戏在事件树和对话分歧差分上的惊人投入，除了直接提供了多样的对话选项外，同样的事件由主角是否是第一次见到对方/完成对方故事线都有对话差分，还有一些角色由主角当前的善恶值，着衣是否是可爱系也能产生不同对话。游戏主角作为有着特别的“共鸣系统”能力的机械人，还可以汲取他人的感情反应来永久强化自身能力。除了剧情对话选项直接和他人达成共鸣外，就算是在激烈的战斗中主角也可以夸赞对面旅游向导机械人的异国文化魅力来和对方达成共鸣来强化自身，和商店老版在擂台打架时可以撒娇让他下次把东西卖便宜点，而如果在对战中输给了对方也不会结束游戏而是有独立的战败对话且如果能有第二次见面则还会有复仇战台词。 玩家在这个世界做的每一件事都会直接反馈到自身，而玩家的不同选择也会切实地改变这个世界——在这样一个奇怪又可爱的世界中，真的能体会到作者细致的制作投入带来的沉浸感让人想要去尝试更多事情更多选择。 再说战斗，虽然游戏画风是萌萌哒但这游戏主题就是战斗爽（副标题就叫RobotBattleChampionship机械人格斗大赛），游戏的战斗系统也是做的相当好玩。在回合制的基础上加上了类似光之子的速度条与格子距离概念，搭配游戏中提供的多样的装备效果可以打出很多样的玩法。极速流可以不停地加速自身和给对面降速攻击来达到“一直都是我的回合”，场地人可以给地上铺满虫网把对方困死在原地无法靠近来把对方远程轻松带走，不想动脑了也可以选择当个重装大猩猩给自己上个无法被撼动的buff站桩输出。游戏的战斗广度深度都不错，虽然平衡做的不太好，但游戏难度本身偏低，成型的流派都是可以爽玩的。战斗本身的演出也非常用心，角色有登场动画退场动画，不同技能有不同的动画动作，其中像偶像套的偶像之歌这种还有一套舞蹈动作，进入部分异常状态也会直接改变角色的待机动作...这个工作量，这真的是单人制作的游戏吗！？ 虽然是在年末才玩到，但本作但这绝对是我在2025年玩到最印象深刻的游戏之一了。想起来2025我最喜欢的游戏DOLLS NEST那边也是暖暖机娘游戏但风格却和这边大相径庭...不管怎么说，本作不仅是有着一个萌萌哒的软萌画风，游戏在质量面上也是完全过硬——不止是角色们可爱，还是有着一个能让人沉浸进去的一个可爱的世界的游戏，强烈推荐。

Extremely earnest and charming character-raising RPG that I enjoyed 100%ing over 20 hours! It took me about 6 hours for my first playthrough, then 2-3 for subsequent ones - it fit very perfectly in the evenings after work. Robot Girl's Dream has very funny writing and heartfelt character arcs that feel almost like a morning cartoon in energy - it's lighthearted with lots of chances to act like a total gremlin (I love Thin's personality) yet still very sweet and endearing. There's plenty to discover through repeated playthroughs, and I love how characters appear in multiple arcs as well as the main RPG section - it really makes the world feel vibrant. The RPG section is also very fun - I loved how the combat felt like puzzle-solving, repeatedly retrying battles attempting to figure out the right series of actions to barely claim victory, and as I played the game more, I was able to build up more and more successful strategies. Mamo and Bestra are my favorites!

Though some bits and pieces aren't translated very well (usually names of skills/effects and very rarely in the actual story), this is a very fun story to read through with many character arc's to explore. As someone else described it, the earnestness of this game's writing had me hollering out loud with laughter more than once and did a fantastic job of endearing the characters to me. The gameplay for the fights you get into in this are actually quite interesting, though they can be unforgiving to people playing it for the first time, as they get a general handle on the various ways you can power-up Thin, the robot you play as. If you get this, don't let yourself get discouraged if you get a game over, since there are many ways to progress through the story and you can fast forward through any previously read text.

唉......游戏的BGM真的很一言难尽，真的很败坏我对游戏的好感，其实我真的挺喜欢这个游戏的......如果是作者自己创作的，那我觉得真的要考虑提升一下水平了，我完全不介意简陋的歌曲，但至少是能听下去的旋律，或者去魔王魂之类的地方定制一些音乐也是可以的......加油。 はあ…ゲームのBGMが本当に何とも言えない感じで、ゲームへの好感度をかなり損なってしまいました。実はこのゲーム自体は結構好きなんですけど……。もし作者さんが自作されているなら、そろそろレベルアップを真剣に考えたほうがいいと思います。私はシンプルな曲でも全く構いませんが、せめて聴いていられるメロディーであってほしいです。あるいは「魔王魂」のようなサイトで音楽をカスタムオーダーするのも手だと思います……。頑張ってください。 Sigh… the game's BGM is really hard to put into words—it honestly ruins a lot of my goodwill toward the game. I actually do like this game quite a bit, though… If the composer is the developer themselves, I really think they should consider stepping up their game. I don't mind simple or basic tunes at all, but at least they should have a melody that’s listenable. Alternatively, they could customize music from sites like Maoudamashii… Hang in there.

Cute game with a cute cast featuring 1v1 fights using customizable parts as you fight and train your way to the top of a fighting tournament for robots.
Female protagonist. Romantic interactions between girls can happen (some with endings) but are not a major focus of the game.
Robot Girl’s Dream: Robot Battle Championship is a 2D RPG where a robot girl with amnesia competes in intense robot battles, blending heartfelt storytelling with fun tournament gameplay.

2D RPG/adventure/simulation about a robot girl’s journey of growth and self-discovery after losing her memories. It blends life sim, visual novel, and turn-based RPG elements, and it works really well
Game name says it all.
A cute life simulator combining a visual novel and an RPG. You have to manage the life of a robot girl who has lost her memory. Pleasant cartoon style, interesting story and charming characters.
This game gets an A+ for starring a cute and funny protagonist!
